executive_summary: Document analysed successfully. The contract structure reveals heavily weighted terms in favour of the vendor. Highest ranked issues: R-002 Penalty or liquidated damages language; R-001 Unilateral termination rights.

high_risks.title: Severe Penalty on Termination
high_risks.explanation: Section 2 specifies that if the Customer terminates early, they must pay a penalty of USD 500,000 without proof of actual damage.
high_risks.why_it_matters: Extremely high fixed penalties can heavily restrict your operational freedom and lock you into the contract.

verification.reasoning: Penalty clauses without proof of damage are treated strictly under Indian Law.
verification.what_the_contract_says: Customer must pay a penalty of USD 500,000.
verification.what_the_law_says: Section 74 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 stipulates that if a sum is named in the contract as the amount to be paid in case of breach, the complaining party is entitled to reasonable compensation not exceeding the named amount.
verification.what_the_system_inferred: The USD 500,000 may be challenged in court as an unenforceable penalty rather than reasonable liquidated damages.

medium_risks.title: Short Termination Notice
medium_risks.explanation: The contract allows termination with only 15 days notice.
medium_risks.why_it_matters: A short notice period might disrupt your business operations suddenly.

questions_for_lawyer: Is the USD 500,000 penalty considered reasonable compensation under Section 74 of the Indian Contract Act, or an unenforceable penalty?
Can we negotiate the 15-day termination notice to at least 30 or 60 days to ensure business continuity?
